practice_description.medium: Software, web applications, video, data, writing
practice_description.practice_summary: Sam Lavigne creates tools, software, and data-driven artworks that interrogate surveillance, labor, policing, and corporate power. His practice treats data curation, recomposition, and tool-making as primary creative acts.
practice_description.methodology: Lavigne works through what he calls 'Scrapism' — the creative repurposing of found data through web scraping, natural language processing, and computational recomposition. He builds open-source software tools (Videogrep, Runway) that function simultaneously as artworks and as instruments others can use. His process typically involves collecting large datasets from public or institutional sources, then applying algorithmic transformations that reveal hidden patterns or absurdities. He teaches at NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program (ITP), embedding pedagogy into his practice.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Lavigne's practice of building tools that recompose data into new meaning directly models how a graph-curated generative exhibition could function — art emerging from the relational recombination of source material.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes. His tools and datasets function as substrate layers — Videogrep outputs, scraped datasets, and recomposed texts can all serve as raw material for further generative composition.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Partially. While his individual works are often linear transformations, the ecosystem of tools he builds enables relational composition — outputs from one tool feed into others, creating chains of derivation.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Some works are generative-on-demand (Videogrep produces different outputs based on input parameters), but most are not continuously self-recomposing. The tools themselves enable ongoing recomposition by users.

works.title: Videogrep
works.description: Open-source command-line tool that searches through video dialogue transcripts and automatically creates supercuts based on search terms. Widely adopted by artists, journalists, and researchers.
works.relevance: Exemplifies tool-as-artwork and data recomposition as creative act. Its output is inherently relational — meaning emerges from the juxtaposition of found fragments.

works.title: Scrapism (book/methodology)
works.description: A methodology and book teaching web scraping as artistic practice — treating publicly available data as material for creative intervention and political critique.
works.relevance: Provides a theoretical and practical framework for data-as-material that aligns with A(DAI)'s approach to field intelligence gathering and recomposition.

works.title: White Collar Crime Risk Zones
works.description: A predictive policing tool inverted to predict white-collar crime instead of street crime, using financial and corporate data. Created with Francis Tseng and collaborators.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how recomposing institutional data through a different relational frame reveals systemic patterns — a model for graph-based sensemaking.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Lavigne treats tool-making itself as artistic medium. His software tools are not just instruments but artworks that encode editorial and political positions in their design — the protocol is the art.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Videogrep (video recomposition tool), Scrapism methodology, various web-based data tools released as open-source software on GitHub.

commons_orientation.licence_model: Open source (MIT license for most tools)
commons_orientation.commons_summary: Strongly commons-oriented. Nearly all tools are open source on GitHub. His pedagogical practice at NYU ITP further distributes knowledge as commons. The Scrapism methodology is explicitly designed to be adopted and remixed by others.

governance_model.governance_detail: Primarily solo practice with frequent collaborations. Tools are released as open source but maintained primarily by Lavigne. Collaborative projects (like White Collar Crime Risk Zones) use informal collective decision-making.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Works primarily with publicly available data. Scraping practice raises questions about consent that Lavigne addresses critically — his work often highlights the tension between public data and privacy.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship for tools, collaborative for specific projects. Open-source release enables distributed co-authorship through forks and contributions.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Tools like Videogrep produce different outputs each time based on input parameters and source material. The tools themselves are durable infrastructure; individual outputs are ephemeral compositions.

data_materiality.data_sources: Web scrapes of public data, video transcripts, government databases, corporate filings, social media, news archives. Source material varies by project.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Primarily scraped from public sources. Lavigne's practice explicitly engages with the ethics and politics of data provenance — scraping is positioned as a political act that challenges data enclosure.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Not a primary focus. While NLP techniques are used in text processing, the work does not centrally engage with latent/embedding spaces as artistic medium.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes — works span text, video, audio, and data visualization, though not unified through embedding spaces.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Works primarily exist as web applications, command-line tools, and screen-based outputs. Some gallery installations, but the primary mode of encounter is through the browser or terminal.

interoperability.composability: High. Tools are designed as composable command-line utilities with standard input/output. Videogrep outputs video files; data tools output JSON/CSV. Outputs readily serve as inputs for other tools.

technical_approach.stack: Python, JavaScript, FFmpeg, NLP libraries (spaCy, NLTK), web scraping (BeautifulSoup, Selenium), command-line tools, web applications

network_position.scene_affiliation: New York new media art, NYU ITP community, critical tech art, data art, computational journalism intersection. Connected to broader net art and tactical media traditions.
network_position.connections: Everest Pipkin (shared commons/tool-making ethos), various ITP-adjacent artists and technologists

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Lavigne's tools (especially Videogrep) and Scrapism methodology could directly inform A(DAI)'s signal processing pipeline. His practice of tool-as-artwork models how A(DAI)'s infrastructure itself could be exhibited. He could serve as a conversation partner on data ethics and recomposition as creative practice.
